title: How fast did the internet grow?
examples: How many people use the internet?
How fast did the internet grow?
How many people are not online?

explain.say: Your grandparents probably grew up with no internet at all! Now billions of people use it every day. Look at the graph: the line shows how many people were online each year.

draw.text: How fast did the internet grow?

explain.say: Look at the first mark: in 1995, only about 16 million people were online. That is fewer than live in one big city like Lagos or Mumbai today! The line is almost flat here. What do you think happens next?

Whoosh, the line shoots up! See the 2005 mark? One billion people. Look at 2014: three billion, helped by cheap smartphones. The steep part of a line means fast growth. Can you see where it starts to bend?
Near the top the line bends and slows down, like an S. Look at 2024: about 5.5 billion people online. Most people who can easily get online already are. Now, who is still offline?
Great graph reading! Look: about 2.6 billion people, about one in three, are still offline, mostly in villages far from networks. Challenge: what would change in your day without the internet?

faq.q: How many people use the internet?
faq.a: About 5.5 billion people in 2024, around two thirds of everyone on Earth, according to the International Telecommunication Union.
asks: How many internet users are there?

faq.q: How fast did the internet grow?
faq.a: From about 16 million users in 1995 to 1 billion in 2005, 3 billion around 2014 and about 5.5 billion in 2024.
asks: When did the internet get popular?

faq.q: How many people are not online?
faq.a: About 2.6 billion people in 2024, many in rural areas where networks or devices cost too much.
A line that starts flat, rises steeply, then levels off, like a stretched letter S. Many new inventions spread this way.
asks: Why does the graph look like an S?

faq.q: What helped the internet grow so fast?
faq.a: Cheaper computers, then smartphones and mobile networks that reached places with no phone lines at all.
asks: Why did so many people get online?

facts: About 5.5 billion people, roughly 68 percent of the world, used the internet in 2024 (ITU).
The number of internet users passed 1 billion around 2005.

quiz.say: About how many people used the internet in 2024?
quiz.show: About how many people used the internet in 2024?
quiz.why: About 5.5 billion people were online in 2024.

wrong.0: That is a thousand times too small.
wrong.2: There are only about 8 billion people on Earth.

quiz.say: What does the steep part of the graph show?
quiz.show: What does the steep part of the graph show?
quiz.why: A steep line means the number is rising quickly.

wrong.1: No change would be a flat line.
wrong.2: The line never goes down, so people were not leaving.
